properties.community_vision: Cecil County is on the cusp of significant change, with projections of rapid population and household growth by 2030. properties.community_vision: Hampstead is the quintessential American small town. The community is clean, safe and attractive. The residential neighborhoods are quiet and well maintained. While many residents work outside the community, this is “home.” Hampstead is a great place for families. The public schools are excellent and the neighborhoods have very little crime. There are outstanding youth sports programs and a wide range of parks, playgrounds and recreational facilities. Hampstead is an active community. Residents walk, particularly around neighborhoods and on Main Street. While primarily a residential community, Hampstead has a thriving business district. The historic downtown is constantly improving. With many commuters using the Hampstead Bypass, the congestion on Main Street is much reduced. Heavier commercial uses are clustered at the north and south ends of Towns, preserving Hampstead’s “small town” feel. Industrial development is concentrated in and around existing industrial sites. These sites are buffered from the rest of the community. All new construction is held to high standards for design. While large enough to qualify as a “city,” Hampstead is committed to remaining a “town”-- in name and character. It is a community people are proud to call home.

properties.community_vision: Chesapeake City has a distinguishing “sense of place” in terms of our heritage, layout, architecture, and picturesque setting. The C&D is one of busiest canals in the United States, but our community does not rely on commercial shipping, ﬁsheries or manufacturing. Instead, our community is built on being the “Jewel of the Upper Shore” and the unique characteristics that draw people to live and visit Chesapeake City. properties.community_vision: In the coming years, Annapolis will be a more equitable, healthy, and resilient city. It will be a more walkable and connected city where multiple safe and reliable transportation options reduce personal vehicle dependency. It will be a city which prioritizes public investments in its most socially vulnerable communities; a city which expands housing options accessible to residents of all income levels; and a city which grows a community of diverse local entrepreneurs aided by inclusive economic programs and opportunities. Annapolis will be a city which prioritizes the preservation, restoration, maintenance, and enhancement of its natural resources, particularly when planning for new development. It will be a city which ensures that all residents have access to high quality recreational amenities particularly public water access; and it will be a city which values its cultural life through support for arts initiatives, artists and arts organizations, and citywide historic preservation efforts. And Annapolis will be climate ready. Its infrastructure will be designed to withstand or adapt to the impacts from climate change. The city will protect its communities and institutions most at risk of climate impacts; and the city will reduce its carbon emissions through a variety of coordinated policies, programs, and investments.

The plan aims to bolster the local economy by attracting new businesses, particularly in light industrial and tourism sectors, while enhancing residents' quality of life through new community traditions, health services, and recreational opportunities like expanded trail networks. properties.community_vision: The guiding principal for the Town of Oxford is to preserve the current unique small town character of Oxford, strictly regulating and controlling future expansion, while maintaining its historic neighborhoods, its commercial areas, its recreational facilities, its environmentally sensitive areas, its economic stability, and its diversity. properties.community_vision: The community's vision for Perryville is to revitalize its historic 'Olde Towne' area into a vibrant, safe, and desirable place to live and work. Key goals include improving housing and commercial properties, creating a 'Main Street' with active businesses, enhancing public parks and recreational opportunities, and leveraging its strategic location and transit access (MARC train) to foster economic growth and community pride. The plan focuses on making sustained improvements to attract residents, businesses, and tourism, creating a strong sense of place and neighborhood stability.

properties.community_vision: The Town of Pittsville envisions a future that preserves its rural heritage and small-town character while fostering focused growth. The community aims to become more pedestrian-oriented by improving sidewalks and bikeways, concentrating on infill development within its central business and residential districts, and attracting essential services such as a grocery store and medical practices. The vision includes leveraging the town's historic assets and its location near US Route 50 to enhance economic vitality and improve the quality of life for residents.

properties.community_vision: Pocomoke City envisions a future as a safe, thriving, and walkable community with an improved quality of life for its residents. Key projects, like a new central library, aim to create a vibrant hub that connects residents to services and amenities, ultimately decreasing crime and increasing property values.

properties.community_vision: The Town of Port Deposit envisions a future of revitalization and growth, transforming into a regional destination for recreation and heritage tourism. properties.community_vision: Reimagine Middle Branch is a community-driven initiative to reconnect South Baltimore with a system of world-class parks, trails, programs, and economic development plans along the 11-mile shoreline of the Middle Branch of the Patapsco River. By holistically addressing issues of environment, health, and equity, Reimagine Middle Branch strives to realize more than Baltimore’s next great waterfront. This initiative is fundamentally about equity and justice, resilience, and health—a transformation of place supported by new connections, jobs, wealth-generation, and quality of life amenities that extend beyond the built environment.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The plan covers 11+ miles of shoreline along the Middle Branch of the Patapsco River in South Baltimore, encompassing 19 neighborhoods, over 30 parks, and nearly 600 acres of parkland. The study area extends approximately 1.5 miles from the shoreline and includes neighborhoods such as Brooklyn, Curtis Bay, Cherry Hill, Westport, Pigtown, Federal Hill, and Baltimore Peninsula (Port Covington). The shoreline itself stretches from the Maryland Cruise Terminal and Locust Point Marine Terminals on the northeast to the Masonville and Fairfield Marine Terminals on the southeast.

properties.community_vision: The Reisterstown Main Street community envisions a future as a thriving commercial and cultural destination, building on its historic character and vibrant small business community. Key goals include preserving and expanding greenspace and recreational opportunities, such as the Franklin Woodland Trails and Woodley Avenue Park, to enhance walkability, connectivity, and overall quality of life for residents and visitors.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The Reisterstown Main Street Sustainable Community Area is centered along Main Street (MD State Road 140) in Reisterstown, MD. The plan includes an expansion to incorporate two key greenspaces: the 3.79-acre Woodley Avenue Park site, located one block west of Main Street, and the Franklin Woodland Trails network situated behind Franklin Elementary School. properties.community_vision: The Sustainable Community Action Plan is a multi-year investment strategy designed to increase the economic vitality and livability of the community, foster increased prosperity for local households, and improve the health of the surrounding environment. The plan's vision focuses on preserving and enhancing the town's cultural and historic heritage while guiding new growth and development to the downtown and infill areas. Key initiatives aim to make the town more competitive and attractive by improving streetscaping, parking, tree canopy, landscaping, sidewalks, lighting, and building facades, ultimately reinforcing a strong sense of place.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The Rising Sun Sustainable Community Area covers approximately 377 acres within Cecil County and is located entirely within the town's Priority Funding Area. properties.community_vision: Greater Riverdale aspires to evolve into a well-connected, environmentally sustainable, and economically vibrant community. Key goals include protecting and expanding the tree canopy, improving water quality, and redeveloping aging commercial centers. The community aims to create more affordable housing options, improve neighborhood aesthetics through code enforcement and beautification projects, and enhance public safety. By cultivating its distinct cultural heritage and improving access to healthcare and healthy food, Greater Riverdale seeks to improve the overall quality of life for its diverse and growing population.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The Greater Riverdale Sustainable Community area covers approximately 1,863 acres in Prince George’s County. The area includes the Town of Riverdale Park and a significant portion of the former East Riverdale Bladensburg Transforming Neighborhoods Initiative (TNI) area. It is traversed by major roadways including US 1 (Baltimore Avenue), MD 201 (Kenilworth Avenue), and MD 410 (East-West Highway). The Plan should be flexible enough to be updated regularly and renewed every five years as the community envisions new goals.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The plan for Rock Hall, a waterfront community in Kent County with a year-round population of approximately 1,200, centers on its environmental and economic assets. properties.area_geographic_summary: The City of Salisbury Sustainable Community Area covers approximately 2,958 acres within the City of Salisbury in Wicomico County. Key features include the Downtown district centered around Main Street, the Wicomico River which flows through the city, and various neighborhoods such as the Camden neighborhood. The town seeks to foster economic vitality by supporting its existing businesses and attracting new services, including medical facilities and more fresh food options, through smart growth principles that focus on infill development and protect the natural environment of the Nanticoke River.

A key goal is to attract new full-time residents by improving housing and amenities, ensuring the island remains a viable and resilient place to live for future generations.

Key priorities include upgrading aging water and sewer infrastructure, improving pedestrian connectivity through sidewalk expansion, expanding parks and recreational opportunities, and increasing citizen engagement through improved communication and technology. The town seeks to build its capacity to manage growth effectively, ensuring Smithsburg remains a healthy, safe, and desirable place to live, work, and visit.

The town aims to strengthen its local economy by revitalizing its downtown commercial district, attracting new businesses, and increasing nature-based tourism. Key priorities include upgrading aging infrastructure, diversifying the housing stock to attract new residents and support the workforce, enhancing recreational opportunities, and improving the overall quality of life. Through strategic planning and partnerships, Snow Hill aspires to be a destination to live, work, and visit, celebrated for its strong sense of community and well-preserved heritage.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The Snow Hill Sustainable Community area covers approximately 1,845 acres within the Town of Snow Hill, the County Seat of Worcester County. Situated on the bank of the Pocomoke River and surrounded by the Pocomoke Forest, the area is defined by its significant historic character, with about 80% of the town designated as a Historic District. properties.community_vision: The Town of St. Michaels envisions a future that preserves its historic character, waterfront access, and small-town quality of life while proactively addressing modern challenges. The community aims to mitigate the impacts of sea level rise, improve essential infrastructure like water systems and broadband internet, and support a diverse local economy. This vision includes diversifying beyond tourism to attract more basic services for residents, enhancing pedestrian safety and alternative transportation, and ensuring a range of housing options. St. Michaels aspires to remain a safe, walkable, and attractive community with robust social, recreational, and cultural amenities for all residents.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The St. Michaels Sustainable Community area covers approximately 187 acres within Talbot County, encompassing the town's corporate limits. The area is characterized by its significant waterfront access to the Chesapeake Bay and San Domingo Creek, a central town harbor, and a compact, walkable design. It is recognized as a National Register Historic District. A notable feature is the Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum. Key corridors and streets mentioned include Talbot Street (MD Route 33), Mill Street, Dodson Avenue, and Morengo Street.

properties.community_vision: This plan aims specifically to outline the future growth and improvements on the Town of Sudlersville's Capital Improvement Plan. The Town hopes to expand responsibly and at a rate that is sustainable. Through projects like sidewalk improvements, historic building restoration, park rehabilitation, and community centers, the Town hopes to become more than just another 'dot on the map.' While growth is an attractive prospect for the Town, it is important to hold on to its history as well.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The Town of Sudlersville is located in Queen Anne's County, Maryland, and is centrally located near several major cities, including Wilmington, Philadelphia, and Baltimore. The town's zoning is primarily residential and mixed-use, with districts including Town Central Commercial (TCC), Town Residential (TR), Single Family Residential (SF), Commercial Floating Zone (CFZ), and Mixed Use (MU). The plan area is described as approximately 1.11 square miles and includes the Designated Neighborhood of Maple Street.

properties.community_vision: The Suitland-Naylor Road Metro Station Area envisions a future as a vital and livable community, leveraging its strategic location as a gateway to Prince George's County from Washington D.C. The community aims to transform into a vibrant, mixed-use hub centered around its Metro stations, attracting new investment, residents, and businesses. Key priorities include increasing economic vitality through commercial revitalization and workforce development, enhancing livability by improving housing stock and public safety, and increasing prosperity for households by expanding access to fresh food, healthcare, and recreational opportunities. The plan serves as a multi-year investment strategy to create a more sustainable, connected, and thriving place for all residents.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The Suitland-Naylor Road Metro Station Sustainable Community area is an 1,890-acre unincorporated area in Prince George's County, serving as a primary gateway from Washington, D.C. It is strategically located near the I-95/I-495 Capital Beltway and is defined by major thoroughfares such as Suitland Parkway and MD 5 (Branch Avenue). The area encompasses portions of the Hillcrest Heights–Marlow Heights, Silver Hill, and Suitland-Coral Hills neighborhoods. Key landmarks include the Suitland and Naylor Road Metro Stations, the Suitland Federal Center (which houses the U.S. Census Bureau and other federal agencies), The Shops at Iverson, the St. Barnabas Plaza, and the Creative Suitland Arts Center. The area contains significant parkland, including tracts along the Henson Creek and Oxon Run watersheds.

properties.community_vision: Sykesville envisions a future that preserves its unique historic character while fostering a vibrant, economically robust community. The vision includes the continued revitalization of its award-winning Main Street and the strategic redevelopment of key areas like the Warfield Complex into a major mixed-use employment and cultural center. The town aims to enhance connectivity for pedestrians and cyclists, expand recreational opportunities, and maintain a high quality of life, making it a desirable destination to live, work, and visit.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The Town of Sykesville is a 1,040-acre community in Carroll County, Maryland, with a National Register Historic District. Its geography is defined by the Patapsco River and surrounding natural landscapes, including the Hugg-Thomas WMA and Patapsco Valley State Park. Key areas within the town include the Main Street commercial corridor, the historic Warfield Complex located at the town's eastern boundary across Route 32, and several parks such as Millard Cooper Park and Burkett Park.

properties.community_vision: The City of Taneytown seeks a measured and meaningful revitalization of its Sustainable Community Area, focusing on continuing the successes of previous plans. The community's vision is to improve existing park resources, increase connectivity to the historic downtown core through sidewalk and infrastructure upgrades, and foster a vibrant local economy. Key goals include achieving an Arts & Entertainment District designation, enhancing heritage tourism, improving housing conditions through new programs, and making transportation safer and more accessible for pedestrians, bicyclists, and public transit users. This will be achieved through strategic partnerships and a commitment to smart growth principles, ensuring Taneytown remains an attractive place for residents and businesses.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The Taneytown Sustainable Community Area covers approximately 299 acres within the City of Taneytown in Carroll County, MD. The area holds several designations, including being a Main Street community, a National Register Historic District (Carr-1196), part of the Heart of the Civil War Maryland Heritage Area, and located along the Old Main Streets Maryland Scenic Byway. The area encompasses the historic downtown core, which is centered around MD Route 140 and MD Route 194. It includes a high concentration of the city's residential rental properties, three city parks, and is in close proximity to the local elementary and middle schools.

properties.community_vision: Thurmont's vision is to cultivate a sustainable, walkable, and bikeable family-oriented community that preserves its historic downtown character while accommodating steady residential and economic growth. The town aspires to foster a vibrant Main Street with high building occupancy, an engaged citizenry, and a high quality of life supported by well-planned amenities, diverse housing, and robust infrastructure.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The Town of Thurmont is a community of approximately 1,998 acres in Frederick County, MD, nestled in the foothills of the Catoctin Mountains near Cunningham Falls State Park. Its key features include a designated Main Street area, a commercial corridor on Frederick Road, and an extensive trail system, notably the Thurmont Trolley Trail. properties.community_vision: Towson aims to enhance its role as Baltimore County's vibrant urban core and seat of government. This growth is intended to be balanced with environmental goals such as increasing the tree canopy, improving water quality, and mitigating climate change impacts.

The 2024 plan includes a boundary expansion along Bosley Avenue to incorporate sites for the 'Road to Freedom' trail, including the Howard Cooper Memorial Marker, the Bykota Senior Center, and the Pleasant Rest Cemetery.

properties.community_vision: The Town of Trappe aims to transition from a residential commuter town into a more self-sufficient community by revitalizing its town center. The vision prioritizes retaining existing businesses and attracting new small enterprises to provide much-needed local services. properties.area_geographic_summary: The Town of Trappe is a small, rural community on Maryland's Eastern Shore, primarily residential and surrounded by agricultural land. The plan identifies areas for economic improvement along these corridors, older town sections affected by poor stormwater drainage, and an area on Barber Road designated for manufacturing.

properties.community_vision: The Town of Vienna envisions itself as a model Chesapeake Bay community, serving as a gateway to the Nanticoke River. properties.area_geographic_summary: The Waldorf Sustainable Community Area (SCA) covers approximately 11,818 acres. Its boundary incorporates the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC), which is the county's central transit-oriented redevelopment area. The plan also covers existing commercial areas, the Demarr and Berry Industrial Parks, and older residential neighborhoods including St. Charles, Pinefield, and White Oak Village. A portion of the SCA is also designated as a federal Opportunity Zone.

properties.area_geographic_summary: The Town of Westernport is a 564-acre community in Allegany County, Maryland, located at the intersection of Maryland Routes 36 and 135. The city aims to build a tech ecosystem, enhance its urban forestry program, ensure an adequate water supply for growth, attract and retain businesses on Main Street, and improve connectivity for pedestrians and cyclists between downtown, McDaniel College, and surrounding neighborhoods.

The downtown commercial district is centered around Conococheague Street, and the area is traversed by major state highways including Routes 11, 63, and 68.

properties.community_vision: Baltimore County's Master Plan 2030 charts an aspirational course for the next decade, aiming to create livable, healthy communities in harmony with nature, with resilient economies, social equity, and strong regional ties. The plan shifts focus from traditional suburban development to a strategy of "retrofitting" underutilized commercial corridors and aging infrastructure. This involves creating walkable, mixed-use community centers, or "Nodes," to serve as the primary focus for redevelopment and investment. The vision is guided by six principles: a Livable Built Environment, Harmony with Nature, a Resilient Economy, Responsible Regionalism, Inclusive Planning, and a Healthy Community, all intended to ensure Baltimore County remains a safe, healthy, and prosperous place for all residents.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The Baltimore County Master Plan 2030 covers the entirety of Baltimore County, Maryland. A key geographical feature is the Urban Rural Demarcation Line (URDL), established in 1967, which divides the county into distinct urban/suburban and rural areas. The plan reinforces the URDL, focusing growth and infrastructure investment within the line to protect rural resources and agricultural land. With developable land inside the URDL nearly depleted, the plan introduces a redevelopment strategy centered on retrofitting existing suburban landscapes. It identifies specific areas called "Nodes" as prime locations for mixed-use redevelopment and investment. These Nodes are distributed throughout the county, including areas like Towson, Catonsville, Dundalk, Owings Mills, and White Marsh, representing a data-driven approach to guide future growth.

properties.community_vision: A unique geologic landform in Maryland, Sugarloaf Mountain is a defining element of Frederick County’s treasured scenic and rural landscape. The mountain and the area surrounding it possess a sublime beauty and significant biodiversity, where a high-quality environment is maintained. Forestlands, aquatic resources, wildlife habitat, inspiring vistas, and historic resources are valued and protected. Land uses are sensitive to both the natural environment and rural character of the area. Stewardship of the area’s natural assets and cultural resources ensures healthy, resilient, and economically productive lands for current and future generations. As we face climate change challenges, Sugarloaf Mountain and the surrounding landscape provide ecosystem benefits to the residents of both Frederick County and the wider region, enhancing the sustainability of our shared environment.
properties.area_geographic_summary: The Sugarloaf Planning Area covers 19,719 acres in southern Frederick County. Its boundary is bordered by the Monocacy National Battlefield to the north, Interstate 270 to the east, the Monocacy River, Greenfield Road, and a portion of MD 28 (Tuscarora Road) to the west, and Frederick County's southern border with Montgomery County. The area's defining feature is Sugarloaf Mountain, a geologic monadnock rising 800 feet above the surrounding landscape of forestlands, low hills, streams, and agricultural fields. The area includes the Monocacy Natural Resource Management Area (MNRMA) and small historic communities such as Buckeystown, Comus, and Hyattstown.
